audit_findings.title: Open-ended Superfund remediation exposure is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable remediation obligation not recoverable through seller indemnification or insurance would reduce the equity bridge; recurring investigation or remediation spending not already normalized could also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In June 2023, in response to a Special Notice Letter received from the EPA in 2022, BCP Ingredients, Inc. ("BCP"), the Company's subsidiary that operates the site, Syntex, EPA, and the State of Missouri entered into an Administrative Settlement Agreement and Order on Consent (“ASAOC”) for a focused remedial investigation/feasibility study ("RI/FS") under which (a) BCP will conduct a source investigation of potential source(s) of releases of 1,4-dioxane and chlorobenzene at a portion of the site and (b) BCP and Syntex will complete a RI/FS to determine a potential remedy, if any is required.
audit_findings.explanation: The active RI/FS demonstrates a present environmental contingency, but the filings provide no remedy, cost range, allocation, accrual, or expected indemnity recovery. A sufficiently large net obligation could affect value, while the record cannot establish its magnitude or materiality. This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated bridge amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest RI/FS cost range, June 2026 accrual, BCP/Syntex allocation, historical spending included in OE, insurance coverage, indemnity scope, and indemnitor credit assessment; rerun OE and the bridge using the expected net unrecovered amount.

audit_findings.title: A potentially unrecorded multi-employer pension withdrawal claim exists
audit_findings.mechanism: A withdrawal liability triggered by complete or partial withdrawal would be a senior claim requiring a bridge deduction unless its cash effects were already reflected in projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The risks of participation in this multi-employer plan are different from single-employer plans in the following aspects: (a) assets contributed to the multi-employer plan by one employer may be used to provide benefits to employees of other participating employers, (b) if a participating employer stops contributing to the plan, the unfunded obligations of the plan may be borne by the remaining participating employers, and (c) if the Company was to stop participating in its multi-employer plan, the Company would be required to pay that plan an amount based on the underfunded status of the plan, referred to as the withdrawal liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates participation in a critically funded multi-employer plan, but it does not demonstrate an actual withdrawal, probable trigger, assessed claim, or current withdrawal-liability amount. Current contributions are already expensed in OE. The exposure therefore remains contingent on future operational or bargaining decisions.
audit_findings.action: Request current complete- and partial-withdrawal estimates and monitor facility, workforce, and collective-bargaining changes. If withdrawal becomes probable or is initiated, add the expected liability to the bridge and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Cash added at par may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $53.925 million foreign-held cash at 2026-06-30, equal to $1.63/share if entirely excluded; excluding all $63.174 million of cash would reduce value by $1.91/share
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash deemed necessary for operations, committed to foreign reinvestment, or subject to repatriation taxes should be excluded or haircut in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had $61,986 of cash and cash equivalents held by our foreign subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that most cash is foreign-held and that a significant portion is intended for foreign reinvestment, so treating every dollar as distributable is not fully supported. Nevertheless, even removing all cash would lower base value only from $82.58 to approximately $80.67 per share, about 2.3%, and would not change the conclusion relative to the $171.61 market price.
audit_findings.action: Determine June 2026 minimum operating cash, committed reinvestment, and jurisdiction-specific withholding taxes. Apply the resulting haircut in the next bridge update; no conclusion-changing rerun is required on the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain-tax liability is not visible in the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.945 million at 2026-06-30, equal to $0.21/share and 0.25% of the $2.727 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The portion representing future settlement cash not already captured by normalized tax expense would be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We have a liability of $6,731 for uncertain tax positions, including the related interest and penalties, recorded in accordance with ASC 740-10, for which we are unable to reasonably estimate the timing of settlement, if any.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a recorded uncertain-tax liability. Even treating the entire $6.945 million as an incremental bridge deduction would reduce base value from $82.58 to approximately $82.37 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion. The correct deductible portion may be smaller because recognition through tax expense may already affect the OE history.
audit_findings.action: Trace the liability and related interest and penalties through historical OE and expected tax cash flows; deduct only the incremental settlement amount not already captured, and document the immaterial adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Existing unfunded retiree obligations are omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.039 million at 2026-06-30 ($1.128 million postretirement medical plus $0.911 million pension funded-status liability), equal to $0.06/share and 0.075% of the $2.727 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Existing obligations for benefits already earned are senior claims that would reduce the equity bridge to the extent future benefit payments are not already captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The liability recorded in other long-term liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 was $1,122 and $1,522, respectively, and the plans are not funded.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates these recorded obligations, but their combined scale is immaterial: a full incremental deduction would reduce base value by only about $0.06 per share. Historical medical-plan payments have also been less than $0.2 million annually, reinforcing that this omission cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 funded status and whether projected OE includes benefit payments against these obligations; record any non-duplicative bridge deduction in the next rerun.
